assertions.name: A6_EM_present_isospin_asymmetry_absent
assertions.source: Z penalty positive in all 3 pairs, 1.71-1.83x too strong; sign inverted at 6He/6Li

description: Diagnoses the 4He binding spike across A=2..6, newly computable via a sparse row-chunked Markov trace (validated against the dense n=12 engine to 1e-12, then run at n=15 and n=18). THE SHORTFALL IS NOT MONOTONE: 4He is a singular outlier at 2.76x where every other A>=3 isotope sits in 1.06..1.89x, exceeding the next-worst by 1.46x. This corrects qou-38i9's '3.4693x' headline, which is B(4He)/B(2H) — a ratio pairing the model's worst undershoot with its only overshoot. THE SPIKE IS AN INVERTED STAGGER, NOT A MISSING PEAK: the B/A second difference has the opposite sign to AME at A=3 (+0.6785 vs -1.2658), A=4 (-0.3880 vs +2.9042) and A=5 (+0.3679 vs -0.6910) — the model peaks at odd A where physics peaks at even A, so nature's pairing enhancement of even-even nuclei is sign-reversed here. It is not an artifact of atom_gen_chains' alternating ordering: grouping gives d2(4) = -0.2915, still negative. CHANNEL PURITY HOLDS ONLY ON THE CHAIN: band_between(0,2) touches generators 2,3,4,5 = strong(n0), intra(n1), EM(n1), strong(n1), so any non-adjacent bond is channel-mixed by construction, and restricting to the pure-strong chain moves the AME comparison further away at 5/6 isotopes. EM PRESENT, ISOSPIN ASYMMETRY ABSENT: the model always penalises higher Z (Coulomb-like, 1.71-1.83x too strong where the sign is right) but AME reverses at A=6 where (N-Z)^2 outweighs Coulomb, so the model ranks 6He above 6Li where nature does the reverse. Liquid-drop reading: volume-like yes, Coulomb-like yes, pairing backwards, asymmetry absent.
caveats: ATTRIBUTION CORRECTION TO qou-38i9. That probe presented the two-row collapse (y_lambda = 0 for l(lambda) >= 3 at every n) as a finding. It is a corollary of a theorem this corpus has already proved in Lean: convention D is Wenzl level r = 2 (wenzlLevel_conventionD) and schurPrincipal_eq_zero_iff gives s_lambda = 0 <=> l(lambda) > r. What was new is only the application — nobody had used it to collapse H_12. The measurements stand; the framing did not.

n=12, n=15 and n=18 weights are RECONSTRUCTED from the closed form y_(n-k,k) = [n-2k+1]_q / Z, since no y_lambda source exists above n=9. Verified against load_cost at n=6 and n=9 and cross-checked wherever an H_6/H_9 counterpart exists, but every number at A>=4 inherits that reconstruction.

Bond insertion order is worth 11% at A=3 and 38-40% at A=4 (qou-38i9). Everything here uses production's interleaved order throughout, so the comparison is internally consistent, but absolute B values are convention-dependent at that level. The staggering INVERSION is a sign result and survives both orderings tested; the magnitudes should not be quoted without the convention.

5He, 5Li and 6He are particle-unstable in nature (5He and 5Li are resonances). Their AME binding energies are still well defined and used here only for B/A trend and isobar-ordering comparisons, not as stability claims. The A=6 isobar comparison that carries the asymmetry finding is 6He vs 6Li, both of which are bound.
